featured.title: Who's Paying for the Grid Transition?
featured.subtitle: Australian electricity network costs, source data to dashboard
featured.problem: Australian network charges rose sharply into 2026, but the data explaining why is scattered across dozens of regulator spreadsheets, one per network per year.
featured.approach: Built the whole chain: Python ingestion into PostgreSQL, dbt transformations into six tested marts, then a five-page Power BI report version-controlled as TMDL and PBIR.
points: 18 regulated networks, 2006 to 2024, from AER, AEMO and state regulator sources
74 DAX measures over a star schema, with red/amber/green thresholds computed from the data rather than hardcoded
80 dbt tests, and every known gap in the source data is stated on the page instead of hidden
Rebuilt as an interactive site anyone can open, plus a verification script that recomputes all 35 headline figures in SQL and checks them against what the page renders

featured.title: Commercial + Fulfilment Analytics
featured.subtitle: Medallion pipeline to a 9-page executive dashboard
featured.problem: Operational dashboards report late deliveries and discounts as counts. Commercial teams need those priced in dollars against net profit before they can act on them.
featured.approach: Databricks medallion pipeline (Bronze to Silver to Gold) feeding a conformed star schema, served through Snowflake into a version-controlled Power BI report.
points: 180,519 order lines across 2 fact tables and 9 conformed dimensions
Activity-based cost-to-serve model turning delivery risk and trade spend into net profit impact
Three What-If scenario sliders (freight surcharge, MOQ threshold, rebate shift) cascading live through the model
Market-level row-level security, row-count and foreign-key reconciliation, and Performance Analyzer profiling
A cohort retention bug found and fixed along the way, where a blunt filter was wiping row context and reporting retention rates of 499% to 1775%

featured.title: Polimap, geo-analytics platform
featured.subtitle: Master's capstone, High Distinction
featured.problem: Decision-makers needed Australian electoral and census data as maps and charts they could interrogate, not as raw statistical releases.
featured.approach: Reproducible ETL into PostgreSQL and PostGIS, a FastAPI backend, and a React and Leaflet front end serving maps, charts and tables.
points: Relational schema design and download, clean, standardise, load pipelines producing join-ready tables
Data quality controls for uniqueness, referential integrity and coverage
Role-based access control, and stakeholder demos and handover documentation delivered under NDA
featured.note: Source stays private under the client NDA. Happy to walk through the architecture in a call.
